- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for reversal.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast rise to 3–4% after spike, then allow gradual mean reversion.
- If 3+ consecutive days of high sentiment + rising prices, model often fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment cools.
- Model underestimates true mean reversion in 30-day horizon — if 10+ days of high prices, forecast should be capped at 10–15% below peak to reflect mean reversion.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out — use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
- If true outcome shows sharp drop after spike, model often fails to anticipate — add 1–2% downward bias in next 3–5 days if sentiment turns negative.
- Model tends to lag in 30-day horizon — if true outcome is rising, forecast should be 1–2% ahead of actual; if falling, 1–2% behind — adjust based on sentiment momentum.
